source.description: Test vectors for argparse4j 0.9.0 text algorithms as used by signal-cli 0.14.7: line-break segmentation (java.text line BreakIterator), justification (TextHelper.adjustSpace), paragraph wrapping (TextHelper.wrap), help rows (TextHelper.printHelp), usage/help layout, parse semantics and error messages, and 'Did you mean' suggestions. Every expected value was produced offline by executing the bundled jars; nothing was typed by hand.
source.jvm: OpenJDK 25.0.5+8 (Temurin), LANG=C.UTF-8, COLUMNS unset unless stated, no controlling terminal
generation: Synthetic parsers: ArgumentParsers.newFor(prog, DefaultSettings.VERSION_0_9_0_DEFAULT_SETTINGS).terminalWidthDetection(false).defaultFormatWidth(width).locale(Locale.ROOT) (the configuration signal-cli uses, except that the width is pinned instead of detected).

Each parse case emulates parseArgsOrFail: parseArgs(argv); on a help screen exit=0 and stdout is what the help action printed; on ArgumentParserException exit=1 and stderr is handleError(e) output; on success exit=0 and attrs is the resulting namespace.
wrap/adjust_space/help_rows call the public static helpers TextHelper.wrap, TextHelper.adjustSpace and TextHelper.printHelp with ASCIITextWidthCounter.
segmentation uses java.text.BreakIterator.getLineInstance() (default locale en_US), iterating first()/next().
levenshtein calls the private ArgumentParserImpl.levenshtein(input, candidate) by reflection.

signal_cli_parser / suggestions with parser 'signal-cli ...': the real parser from org.asamk.signal.App.buildArgumentParser(null) (no config file), obtained by reflection; width 75. Every error/help case was cross-checked against the 0.14.7 binary (identical stderr/stdout apart from DEBUG/TRACE log lines caused by -v in some argv); the binary additionally prints the logging pre-parser's help block before any help output (see spec section 7.4).
signal_cli_other_widths: same, in child JVMs with COLUMNS=45/65/105 (format width = COLUMNS-5); top_help checked byte-for-byte against the binary's --help output after the logging block.

line_break.dfa was learned black-box from BreakIterator (no JDK source read) and verified: 0 mismatches on all 883,708,280 strings of length <= 8 over one representative per class, on 2,000,000 random ASCII strings of length <= 60, and on every segmentation vector here.

conventions.strings: Exact text. Line separator is \n. JSON escapes are used for control and non-ASCII characters.
conventions.definition: Parser definitions list arguments in declaration order. names: option strings, or a single name without leading '-' for a positional. action: store (default), store_true, count. type: string (default), int (Java Integer), long (Java Long), double (Java Double), boolean (Java Boolean.valueOf), enum_string:<Enum> (match by display string, values in enum_values), enum_name:<Enum> (match by constant name, names in enum_names). nargs absent = exactly one value (not a list); integer n = exactly n values (list); '?', '*', '+'. default_text is the Java toString() of the default, which is what help shows. mutex_group is an index into mutex_groups. subparsers.parsers are in declaration order.
conventions.attrs: Namespace after a successful parse: dest -> value. Lists are arrays; enum values are their display string; doubles are JSON numbers (NaN/Infinity as strings). Keys are dests (option name without prefix, '-' replaced by '_', or the explicit dest).
conventions.segments: Concatenating segments gives the text back. A break opportunity exists only between consecutive segments.

classes.W: every ASCII character not listed below: letters, and # & * + / < = > @ \ ^ _ ` | ~
classes.S: space, U+007F, and C0 controls other than those in B and R

line_break.segmentation_rule: From the current position run the DFA from state 0 over successive characters until a missing transition or end of text; the next break is after the last character at which the DFA was in an accepting state (state 0 is never re-entered, every first transition lands in an accepting state, so this always advances). End of text is always a break.

            [--big-dbl BIG_DBL] [--boolv {true,false}]
            [--choice {read,viewed}] [--int-choice {1,2,3}]
            [-o {plain-text,json}] [--trust {always,on-first-use,never}]
            [--enum-name {PLAIN_TEXT,JSON}] [-g [GROUP_ID [GROUP_ID ...]]]
            [--plus PLUS [PLUS ...]] [--opt [OPT]] [--two A B]
            [--three X X X] [--multi-meta [FIRST [REST ...]]]
            [--str-def STR_DEF] [--list-def [LIST_DEF [LIST_DEF ...]]]
            [--empty-help-def EMPTY_HELP_DEF] --req REQ [-x EXX] first
            [rest [rest ...]]

A test parser exercising every option  kind. The description is wrapped and
justified like any other paragraph.

positional arguments:
  first                  First positional.
  rest                   Remaining positionals.

named arguments:
  -h, --help             show this help message and exit
  -s STRING, --string STRING
                         A plain string option.
  -b, --bool-flag        A store-true flag. (default: false)
  -v, --verbose          Countable flag. (default: 0)
  --int INT              32-bit integer with default. (default: 5)
  --long LONG            64-bit integer.
  -t DBL, --dbl DBL      Double with default. (default: 3.0)
  --big-dbl BIG_DBL      (default: 1.0E10)
  --boolv {true,false}   Boolean-valued option.
  --choice {read,viewed}
                         String choices.
  --int-choice {1,2,3}
  -o {plain-text,json}, --output {plain-text,json}
                         Enum by toString. (default: json)
  --trust {always,on-first-use,never}
                         Choose when to trust new identities. (default: on-
                         first-use)
  --enum-name {PLAIN_TEXT,JSON}
                         Enum by constant name.
  -g [GROUP_ID [GROUP_ID ...]], --group-id [GROUP_ID [GROUP_ID ...]], --group [GROUP_ID [GROUP_ID ...]]
                         Zero or more.
  --plus PLUS [PLUS ...]
                         One or more.
  --opt [OPT]            Zero or one.
  --two A B              Exactly two.
  --three X X X          Exactly three, one metavar.
  --multi-meta [FIRST [REST ...]]
  --str-def STR_DEF      String default. (default: hello world)
  --list-def [LIST_DEF [LIST_DEF ...]]
                         List default. (default: [a, b])
  --empty-help-def EMPTY_HELP_DEF
                         (default: x)
  --req REQ              A required option.
  -x EXX                 Short only with dest.

Epilog paragraph one.
Epilog paragraph two  is  long  enough  to  need  wrapping  at the narrower
widths used here.

subcommand_help.send:
usage: signal-cli send [-h] [-g [GROUP_ID [GROUP_ID ...]]]
                  [-u [USERNAME [USERNAME ...]]]
                  [--note-to-self] [--notify-self]
                  [-a [ATTACHMENT [ATTACHMENT ...]]]
                  [--view-once] [-e]
                  [--mention [MENTION [MENTION ...]]]
                  [--text-style [TEXT_STYLE [TEXT_STYLE ...]]]
                  [--quote-timestamp QUOTE_TIMESTAMP]
                  [--quote-author QUOTE_AUTHOR]
                  [--quote-message QUOTE_MESSAGE]
                  [--quote-mention [QUOTE_MENTION [QUOTE_MENTION ...]]]
                  [--quote-attachment [QUOTE_ATTACHMENT [QUOTE_ATTACHMENT ...]]]
                  [--quote-text-style [QUOTE_TEXT_STYLE [QUOTE_TEXT_STYLE ...]]]
                  [--sticker STICKER]
                  [--preview-url PREVIEW_URL]
                  [--preview-title PREVIEW_TITLE]
                  [--preview-description PREVIEW_DESCRIPTION]
                  [--preview-image PREVIEW_IMAGE]
                  [--story-timestamp STORY_TIMESTAMP]
                  [--story-author STORY_AUTHOR]
                  [--edit-timestamp EDIT_TIMESTAMP]
                  [--no-urgent] [--voice-note] [-m MESSAGE |
                  --message-from-stdin]
                  [recipient [recipient ...]]

positional arguments:
  recipient              Specify   the   recipients'   phone
                         number.

named arguments:
  -h, --help             show this help message and exit
  -g [GROUP_ID [GROUP_ID ...]], --group-id [GROUP_ID [GROUP_ID ...]], --group [GROUP_ID [GROUP_ID ...]]
                         Specify the recipient group ID.
  -u [USERNAME [USERNAME ...]], --username [USERNAME [USERNAME ...]]
                         Specify the  recipient  username or
                         username link.
  --note-to-self         Send the message to self.
  --notify-self          If     self     is      part     of
                         recipients/groups  send   a  normal
                         message, not a sync message.
  -m MESSAGE, --message MESSAGE
                         Specify the message to be sent.
  --message-from-stdin   Read  the  message   from  standard
                         input.
  -a [ATTACHMENT [ATTACHMENT ...]], --attachment [ATTACHMENT [ATTACHMENT ...]]
                         Add an attachment. Can  be either a
                         file path or a  data  URI. Data URI
                         encoded  attachments   must  follow
                         the RFC 2397.  Additionally  a file
                         name can be added, e.g. data:<MIME-
                         TYPE>;filename=<FILENAME>;base64,
                         <BASE64 ENCODED DATA>.
  --view-once            Send the  message  as  a  view once
                         message
  -e, --end-session, --endsession
                         Clear session  state  and  send end
                         session message.
  --mention [MENTION [MENTION ...]]
                         Mention   another    group   member
                         (syntax:              start:length:
                         recipientNumber).  Unit   of  start
                         and length  is  UTF-16  code units,
                         NOT Unicode code points.
  --text-style [TEXT_STYLE [TEXT_STYLE ...]]
                         Style parts  of  the  message  text
                         (syntax: start:length:STYLE).  Unit
                         of start and length  is UTF-16 code
                         units, NOT Unicode code points.
  --quote-timestamp QUOTE_TIMESTAMP
                         Specify   the   timestamp    of   a
                         previous    message     with    the
                         recipient or group  to  add a quote
                         to the new message.
  --quote-author QUOTE_AUTHOR
                         Specify the  number  of  the author
                         of the original message.
  --quote-message QUOTE_MESSAGE
                         Specify   the   message    of   the
                         original message.
  --quote-mention [QUOTE_MENTION [QUOTE_MENTION ...]]
                         Quote  with   mention   of  another
                         group member (syntax: start:length:
                         recipientNumber)
  --quote-attachment [QUOTE_ATTACHMENT [QUOTE_ATTACHMENT ...]]
                         Specify  the  attachments   of  the
                         original      message      (syntax:
                         contentType[:filename[:
                         previewFile]]),  e.g.   'audio/aac'
                         or             'image/png:test.png:
                         /tmp/preview.jpg'.
  --quote-text-style [QUOTE_TEXT_STYLE [QUOTE_TEXT_STYLE ...]]
                         Quote  with  style   parts  of  the
                         message text (syntax: start:length:
                         STYLE)
  --sticker STICKER      Send     a     sticker     (syntax:
                         stickerPackId:stickerId)
  --preview-url PREVIEW_URL
                         Specify  the  url   for   the  link
                         preview (the  same  url  must  also
                         appear in the message body).
  --preview-title PREVIEW_TITLE
                         Specify  the  title  for  the  link
                         preview (mandatory).
  --preview-description PREVIEW_DESCRIPTION
                         Specify  the  description  for  the
                         link preview (optional).
  --preview-image PREVIEW_IMAGE
                         Specify  the  image  file  for  the
                         link preview (optional).
  --story-timestamp STORY_TIMESTAMP
                         Specify the  timestamp  of  a story
                         to reply to.
  --story-author STORY_AUTHOR
                         Specify the  number  of  the author
                         of the story.
  --edit-timestamp EDIT_TIMESTAMP
                         Specify   the   timestamp    of   a
                         previous    message     with    the
                         recipient  or  group   to  send  an
                         edited message.
  --no-urgent            Send  the   message   without   the
                         urgent    flag,    so    no    push
                         notification is  triggered  for the
                         recipient. The  message  will still
                         be delivered  in  real-time  if the
                         recipient's app is active.
  --voice-note           Mark  audio  attachments  as  voice
                         notes. Voice  notes  are  displayed
                         inline in Signal clients.
subcommand_help.receive:
usage: signal-cli receive [-h] [-t TIMEOUT]
                  [--max-messages MAX_MESSAGES]
                  [--ignore-attachments] [--ignore-stories]
                  [--ignore-avatars] [--ignore-stickers]
                  [--send-read-receipts]

named arguments:
  -h, --help             show this help message and exit
  -t TIMEOUT, --timeout TIMEOUT
                         Number of seconds  to  wait for new
                         messages (negative  values  disable
                         timeout)
  --max-messages MAX_MESSAGES
                         Maximum  number   of   messages  to
                         receive, before returning.
  --ignore-attachments   Don’t   download   attachments   of
                         received messages.
  --ignore-stories       Don’t receive  story  messages from
                         the server.
  --ignore-avatars       Don't download avatars  of received
                         messages.
  --ignore-stickers      Don't  download  sticker  packs  of
                         received messages.
  --send-read-receipts   Send   read   receipts    for   all
                         incoming    data    messages    (in
                         addition to  the  default  delivery
                         receipts)

usage: signal-cli updateGroup [-h] [-g GROUP_ID] [-n NAME]
                  [-d DESCRIPTION] [-a AVATAR]

                  [--set-permission-send-messages {every-member,only-admins}]
                  [-e EXPIRATION]
                  [--member-label-emoji MEMBER_LABEL_EMOJI]
                  [--member-label MEMBER_LABEL]

named arguments:
  -h, --help             show this help message and exit
  -g GROUP_ID, --group-id GROUP_ID, --group GROUP_ID
                         Specify the group ID.
  -n NAME, --name NAME   Specify the new group name.
  -d DESCRIPTION, --description DESCRIPTION
                         Specify the new group description.
  -a AVATAR, --avatar AVATAR
                         Specify a  new  group  avatar image
                         file
  -m [MEMBER [MEMBER ...]], --member [MEMBER [MEMBER ...]]
                         Specify one or more  members to add
                         to the group
  -r [REMOVE_MEMBER [REMOVE_MEMBER ...]], --remove-member [REMOVE_MEMBER [REMOVE_MEMBER ...]]
                         Specify  one  or  more  members  to
                         remove from the group
  --admin [ADMIN [ADMIN ...]]
                         Specify  one  or  more  members  to
                         make a group admin
  --remove-admin [REMOVE_ADMIN [REMOVE_ADMIN ...]]
                         Specify  one  or  more  members  to
                         remove group admin privileges
  --ban [BAN [BAN ...]]  Specify one or more  members to ban
                         from joining the group
  --unban [UNBAN [UNBAN ...]]
                         Specify  one  or  more  members  to
                         remove from the ban list
  --reset-link           Reset group  link  and  create  new
                         link password
  --link {enabled,enabled-with-approval,disabled}
                         Set  group  link   state,  with  or
                         without admin approval
  --set-permission-add-member {every-member,only-admins}
                         Set permission  to  add  new  group
                         members
  --set-permission-edit-details {every-member,only-admins}
                         Set  permission   to   edit   group
                         details
  --set-permission-send-messages {every-member,only-admins}
                         Set permission to send messages
  -e EXPIRATION, --expiration EXPIRATION
                         Set  expiration  time  of  messages
                         (seconds)
  --member-label-emoji MEMBER_LABEL_EMOJI
                         Specify the  emoji  for  the member
                         label.
  --member-label MEMBER_LABEL
                         Specify the string  for  the member
                         label.

subcommand_help.send:
usage: signal-cli send [-h] [-g [GROUP_ID [GROUP_ID ...]]] [-u [USERNAME [USERNAME ...]]]
                  [--note-to-self] [--notify-self] [-a [ATTACHMENT [ATTACHMENT ...]]] [--view-once]
                  [-e] [--mention [MENTION [MENTION ...]]]
                  [--text-style [TEXT_STYLE [TEXT_STYLE ...]]] [--quote-timestamp QUOTE_TIMESTAMP]
                  [--quote-author QUOTE_AUTHOR] [--quote-message QUOTE_MESSAGE]
                  [--quote-mention [QUOTE_MENTION [QUOTE_MENTION ...]]]
                  [--quote-attachment [QUOTE_ATTACHMENT [QUOTE_ATTACHMENT ...]]]
                  [--quote-text-style [QUOTE_TEXT_STYLE [QUOTE_TEXT_STYLE ...]]] [--sticker STICKER]
                  [--preview-url PREVIEW_URL] [--preview-title PREVIEW_TITLE]
                  [--preview-description PREVIEW_DESCRIPTION] [--preview-image PREVIEW_IMAGE]
                  [--story-timestamp STORY_TIMESTAMP] [--story-author STORY_AUTHOR]
                  [--edit-timestamp EDIT_TIMESTAMP] [--no-urgent] [--voice-note] [-m MESSAGE |
                  --message-from-stdin] [recipient [recipient ...]]

positional arguments:
  recipient              Specify the recipients' phone number.

named arguments:
  -h, --help             show this help message and exit
  -g [GROUP_ID [GROUP_ID ...]], --group-id [GROUP_ID [GROUP_ID ...]], --group [GROUP_ID [GROUP_ID ...]]
                         Specify the recipient group ID.
  -u [USERNAME [USERNAME ...]], --username [USERNAME [USERNAME ...]]
                         Specify the recipient username or username link.
  --note-to-self         Send the message to self.
  --notify-self          If self is part of  recipients/groups  send  a  normal  message, not a sync
                         message.
  -m MESSAGE, --message MESSAGE
                         Specify the message to be sent.
  --message-from-stdin   Read the message from standard input.
  -a [ATTACHMENT [ATTACHMENT ...]], --attachment [ATTACHMENT [ATTACHMENT ...]]
                         Add an attachment. Can be  either  a  file  path  or  a  data URI. Data URI
                         encoded attachments must follow the RFC  2397. Additionally a file name can
                         be added, e.g.  data:<MIME-TYPE>;filename=<FILENAME>;base64,<BASE64 ENCODED
                         DATA>.
  --view-once            Send the message as a view once message
  -e, --end-session, --endsession
                         Clear session state and send end session message.
  --mention [MENTION [MENTION ...]]
                         Mention another group  member  (syntax: start:length:recipientNumber). Unit
                         of start and length is UTF-16 code units, NOT Unicode code points.
  --text-style [TEXT_STYLE [TEXT_STYLE ...]]
                         Style parts of  the  message  text  (syntax:  start:length:STYLE).  Unit of
                         start and length is UTF-16 code units, NOT Unicode code points.
  --quote-timestamp QUOTE_TIMESTAMP
                         Specify the timestamp of a previous message  with the recipient or group to
                         add a quote to the new message.
  --quote-author QUOTE_AUTHOR
                         Specify the number of the author of the original message.
  --quote-message QUOTE_MESSAGE
                         Specify the message of the original message.
  --quote-mention [QUOTE_MENTION [QUOTE_MENTION ...]]
                         Quote  with  mention  of   another   group  member  (syntax:  start:length:
                         recipientNumber)
  --quote-attachment [QUOTE_ATTACHMENT [QUOTE_ATTACHMENT ...]]
                         Specify the attachments  of  the  original  message  (syntax: contentType[:
                         filename[:previewFile]]),   e.g.   'audio/aac'    or   'image/png:test.png:
                         /tmp/preview.jpg'.
  --quote-text-style [QUOTE_TEXT_STYLE [QUOTE_TEXT_STYLE ...]]
                         Quote with style parts of the message text (syntax: start:length:STYLE)
  --sticker STICKER      Send a sticker (syntax: stickerPackId:stickerId)
  --preview-url PREVIEW_URL
                         Specify the url for the link preview (the  same url must also appear in the
                         message body).
  --preview-title PREVIEW_TITLE
                         Specify the title for the link preview (mandatory).
  --preview-description PREVIEW_DESCRIPTION
                         Specify the description for the link preview (optional).
  --preview-image PREVIEW_IMAGE
                         Specify the image file for the link preview (optional).
  --story-timestamp STORY_TIMESTAMP
                         Specify the timestamp of a story to reply to.
  --story-author STORY_AUTHOR
                         Specify the number of the author of the story.
  --edit-timestamp EDIT_TIMESTAMP
                         Specify the timestamp of a previous message  with the recipient or group to
                         send an edited message.
  --no-urgent            Send the message  without  the  urgent  flag,  so  no  push notification is
                         triggered for the recipient. The message  will  still be delivered in real-
                         time if the recipient's app is active.
  --voice-note           Mark audio attachments as voice notes.  Voice notes are displayed inline in
                         Signal clients.
subcommand_help.receive:
usage: signal-cli receive [-h] [-t TIMEOUT] [--max-messages MAX_MESSAGES] [--ignore-attachments]
                  [--ignore-stories] [--ignore-avatars] [--ignore-stickers] [--send-read-receipts]

named arguments:
  -h, --help             show this help message and exit
  -t TIMEOUT, --timeout TIMEOUT
                         Number of  seconds  to  wait  for  new  messages  (negative  values disable
                         timeout)
  --max-messages MAX_MESSAGES
                         Maximum number of messages to receive, before returning.
  --ignore-attachments   Don’t download attachments of received messages.
  --ignore-stories       Don’t receive story messages from the server.
  --ignore-avatars       Don't download avatars of received messages.
  --ignore-stickers      Don't download sticker packs of received messages.
  --send-read-receipts   Send read receipts for  all  incoming  data  messages  (in  addition to the
                         default delivery receipts)

usage: signal-cli updateGroup [-h] [-g GROUP_ID] [-n NAME] [-d DESCRIPTION] [-a AVATAR]
                  [-m [MEMBER [MEMBER ...]]] [-r [REMOVE_MEMBER [REMOVE_MEMBER ...]]]
                  [--admin [ADMIN [ADMIN ...]]] [--remove-admin [REMOVE_ADMIN [REMOVE_ADMIN ...]]]

named arguments:
